name: Southeast Peak Standard (Home Lake approach)

ways.name: Upper Dungeness Trail, Camp Handy and Boulder Shelter to the southeast cirque
ways.season: Roughly Jul-Sep. Snow in the summit couloir into early season is an improvement on the scree that replaces it
ways.notes:
From US-101 near Sequim Bay State Park turn on Louella Road for a mile, then Palo Alto Road for about 5.8 miles, becoming FS Road 28 at the forest boundary. Right on FS 2880 past Dungeness Forks Campground, then left on FS 2870 for 8.7 miles to the Upper Dungeness Trailhead. Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass required at the kiosk.

Trail #833.2 is the shortest and easiest approach. Hike 3.2-3.4 miles and about 600 ft to Camp Handy at roughly 3,100 ft, a riverfront meadow with a cedar-shingle shelter, then take the uphill fork and continue about 3 miles and 1,850 ft to Boulder Camp / Boulder Shelter at 6.3-6.4 miles and roughly 4,890-4,950 ft. The creek there is the most reliable water on the approach.

From Boulder Shelter hike south on the Dungeness / Constance Pass trail, crossing several creeks, toward Home Lake.

ways.name: Home Lake basecamp, from either the Dungeness or the Dosewallips side
ways.notes:
Home Lake at about 5,308-5,330 ft, walled in by Mount Constance and Warrior Peak just below Constance Pass, is the standard basecamp for this climb and it is reachable from two directions: north up the Upper Dungeness / Constance Pass trail at roughly 9.3 miles from the Upper Dungeness Trailhead, or south from the Dosewallips road end over Constance Pass. An Olympic National Park wilderness permit is required.

Camping at Home Lake rather than pushing from Boulder Shelter turns this into a comfortable two-day trip and puts you a mile from the cirque. It is also the camp shared with Mount Fricaba, Mount Mystery and Mount Deception parties, so it is well-used ground with an established site.

From the lake, leave the basin and climb east into the Warrior / Inner Constance cirque through meadow and talus.

priorPrimaryResearch: Paragraph is the Upper Dungeness / Boulder Shelter approach to the SE cirque (v0), called the shortest and easiest; v1 is the Home Lake camp option on the same corridor.

name: South Ridge / Southwest Slope

ways.name: Rainy Pass PCT lot, then cross-country east into the meadow basin and the col toward Cutthroat's southwest peak
ways.notes:
Park at the marked Pacific Crest Trail North trailhead lot on the north side of Rainy Pass at about 4,850 ft, next to the Road 600 turnoff. Leave the PCT almost immediately and strike out cross-country east into open forest, gaining steeply through timber and over downed logs. There is no maintained tread once you leave the PCT.

This is Whistler Mountain above Rainy Pass in Chelan County, not the Whistler Canyon trailhead area near Oroville, which is about 100 miles away and unrelated.

Round trip runs roughly 3.7 miles with about 3,000 ft of gain.

ways.name: The unmarked SR-20 turnout, then a boot path onto the true south ridge at 6,180 ft
ways.notes:
The second option, and the one that reaches the true south ridge. From the unmarked pullout on SR-20 about 3.1 miles east of Rainy Pass, 0.7 mile before the Blue Lake trailhead, at about 5,000 ft, walk back down and along the road shoulder to a boot path that starts at the west edge of a stand of trees.

About 4 miles round trip with roughly 3,000 ft of gain, the same as the PCT option.

priorPrimaryResearch: Prose itself calls Option A (Rainy Pass PCT lot) the most commonly used; that is variant 0.

name: Northwest Shoulder

ways.name: Niederprum Trail #653 to Lone Tree Pass and High Pass
ways.season: late Apr-Jun for snow cover; the line goes later but on more rock
ways.notes:
Niederprum trailhead at the end of Old Mine Road above Darrington. The Moose Creek bridge just past the gate has been closed and barricaded for years, so parties park at the gate, get past the barricade on foot and walk the road roughly a mile and a quarter to the real trailhead — extra distance and gain that older published figures do not include.

Trail #653 switchbacks through forest into the Boulder River Wilderness and reaches 'the flat' at about 3,200 ft, a level clearing on the site of an old mining cabin and the natural rest or camp spot. Beyond it the maintained tread ends and a boot path threads thinning, brushy forest with deadfall.

Above that the route traverses south through moderately dense forest between roughly 4,500 and 4,700 ft to reach a broad snow couloir, which is climbed to Lone Tree Pass at about 5,000 ft. From the pass, traverse east along the ridge and then drop several hundred feet southeast to a small lake and flat meadow — a sheltered bivy. A long rising traverse east below cliff bands then leads to a broad gully up to High Pass at about 6,100 ft, and over it onto the So-Bahli-Ahli (Whitehorse) Glacier.

ways.name: Snow Gulch direct (deep snow only)
ways.season: early season, deep snow burying the brush
ways.notes: A more direct line used by some early-season and ski parties. From the Niederprum trailhead area, follow the old forest-road grade toward Snow Gulch, then ascend the creek drainage. The section between roughly 1,100 and 2,200 ft is a steep bushwhack through slide alder or up the adjacent slabs, and it only makes sense once deep snow has buried the brush. Parties commonly stash skis or boards around 2,500 ft in the old growth for the descent.

priorPrimaryResearch: Niederprum #653 to Lone Tree Pass and High Pass is the standard route, and Snow Gulch is a deep-snow-only variant used by some ski parties.

name: Wild Wild West

ways.name: Road walk from the pullout to the foot of the wall
ways.notes: From Randle, head south and follow the main forest road roughly nineteen miles, then turn off at the signed meadows turning and follow the next road under three miles before turning again onto the last one. That final road is rough and wants high clearance; follow it about two miles until the rock appears, then carry on to the large pullout where the climbers' trail is obvious. From the pullout, simply walk up the road toward the wall and onto its base. There is no cell service on the approach or at the crag.

ways.name: Around the East Face and through the Gap
ways.notes: The other way onto this side of the formation, and the one to use if you are coming from routes on the far side. From the same pullout, take the climbers' trail around the east face of the rock — this trail traverses the whole formation — and pass through the deep gully that splits it, then drop down to the left onto the West Face's base. It is longer than walking up the road but it links the two sides without returning to the car.

priorPrimaryResearch: Walking up the road from the pullout is the direct way to the West Face; variant 1 is for parties coming from routes on the far side.

ways.name: Trail 342 from Long Swamp
ways.notes: This is the easternmost of the high peaks here and by far the least technical, being a trail walk with a very short scramble stapled on the end, so the real work is the drive. Long gravel forest roads out of Loomis reach Long Swamp Campground, where Trail 342 starts and climbs steadily through burned lodgepole and recovering meadow to a camp with water partway up and then out onto open, treeless ridge. A shorter trail comes in from the Cathedral Driveway trailhead a few miles further west but is overgrown in stretches from lack of use, and a third start at Iron Gate involves the roughest driving of the three. Water on the upper trail is limited and seasonal, so carry enough for a long day.

ways.name: Windy Creek trail from Cathedral Driveway
ways.notes: The shortest way up. From the Cathedral Driveway trailhead, a few miles west of Long Swamp on the same road, climb the Windy Creek trail about five miles to its junction with the Windy Peak trail, then go a short distance more to the summit. Some maps wrongly show the trail starting from the Cathedral Driveway trail about half a mile west of the trailhead.

ways.name: Boundary Trail from Iron Gate
ways.notes: The roughest drive of the three. From FR-39, turn onto FR-3900-500 and follow it about six miles to the Iron Gate trailhead; a high-clearance vehicle is recommended and passenger cars are not advised. Hike north on the Boundary Trail toward Sunny Pass and Horseshoe Basin, then take the Windy Peak trail west to the summit scramble.
